page: Amazon Web Services im4gn.xlarge is a storage-optimized virtual instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the arm64 AWS Graviton processor family (ARMv8 Neoverse-N1). The configuration features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with 1 thread per core running at 2.5 GHz, supported by 16.0 GB of memory (4.0 GB per core). CPU cache layout comprises 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. There are no discrete GPUs. Networking throughput provides a baseline bandwidth of 6 Gbps, and the host includes a dedicated 1875 GB NVMe SSD for fast local data access.

Benchmark evaluations reflect the architectural profile of an entry-scale arm64 storage node. Single-core throughput via stress-ng registers 1519.89 points (middle 50%), while multi-core computational throughput delivers 6054.65 points. Standard synthetic metrics place its overall processing output on the lower end, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 3191.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 2682.86. Memory performance displays large-block uncached read speeds of 69.63 GB/sec and write speeds of 33.78 GB/sec. Operational workloads capture 4.92 million operations/sec for Redis SET benchmarks and 4.77 GB/sec for static web serving.

Cost efficiency for the im4gn.xlarge centers on dense, high-throughput local storage coupled with energy-efficient Graviton compute. The 1875 GB NVMe SSD provides strong storage density per compute thread without incurring network-attached storage overhead. While dense localized I/O reduces cost relative to provisioned block volumes, the system trade-off lies in modest compute and memory density, making it less viable for CPU-heavy tasks or massive in-memory databases. Appropriate deployments include distributed databases, log indexing clusters, intermediate ETL buffering, and read/write-heavy cache tiers.
description: Amazon Web Services im4gn.xlarge is a storage-optimized instance operating on the AWS Nitro System, utilizing a 4-core arm64 AWS Graviton processor (Neoverse-N1) clocked at 2.5 GHz alongside 16.0 GB of memory. It features 1875 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD storage and a 6 Gbps baseline network link, with no GPU hardware present. Benchmark results show average single-core CPU throughput (stress-ng 1519.89) alongside lower-tier multi-core marks (PassMark CPU score of 2682.86 and Geekbench multi-core score of 3191.0). Large block memory transfers sustain 69.63 GB/sec read and 33.78 GB/sec write bandwidth, while Redis achieves 4.92 million SET operations per second. Balancing power-efficient Arm cores with large local solid-state capacity, the im4gn.xlarge is suited for I/O-intensive workloads, including distributed database nodes, caching layers, and search index ingestion.
